images.title: Where the mean sits
images.purpose: Compare three small data sets to show that a low outlier puts the mean below the median, balanced data keeps them close, and a high outlier puts the mean above the median.
images.composition: Three short dot plots stacked one above another on the same scale, each with a caption at its left and two small markers; white space between rows.
exact_structure: Three dark grey (#2B2B2B) number lines from 0 to 30, aligned one under another, each with small ticks every 5; only the bottom line has numbered ticks at 0, 10, 20 and 30.

Top row, captioned Low outlier: mean < median: 5 dots, 1 vermilion (#D55E00) dot at 2 and 4 teal (#0072B2) dots at 14, 15, 16 and 18; amber (#E69F00) mean triangle at 13 and reddish purple (#CC79A7) median triangle at 15.

Middle row, captioned Balanced: mean ≈ median: 5 teal dots at 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19, no outlier; the amber mean triangle and the reddish purple median triangle both at 15, the median triangle just under the line and the mean triangle directly under it.
Bottom row, captioned High outlier: mean > median: 5 dots, 4 teal dots at 12, 14, 15 and 16 and 1 vermilion dot at 28; amber mean triangle at 17 and reddish purple median triangle at 15.
The triangles sit just under each line and point up; the median triangle is at 15 in every row.
A small key at the top right: an amber triangle labelled Mean and a reddish purple triangle labelled Median.
rejection: a row with other than 5 dots
the three rows on different scales
a mean triangle on the wrong side of its median triangle
the median triangle not at 15 in every row
images.takeaway: The mean moves towards an outlier; with no outlier, mean and median sit close together at the centre.
images.description: Three dot plots of five values each: a low outlier with mean 13 and median 15, balanced data with both at 15, and a high outlier with mean 17 and median 15.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to say for each row which way the mean has moved, then place the newspaper pages in the right row.

image_decisions.why: Three small rows side by side show the whole rule about mean, median and outliers at once.
